# 01 · At a glance

California is the largest CMS TEAM state by mandated roster: **`r SCOPE_N` hospitals** across **`r SCOPE_CBSA_N` CBSAs**, covering an estimated **6.3 million** Medicare beneficiaries.^11^ California TEAM hospitals show a **55.2%** Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP) penalty rate versus **48.1%** nationally.^6^

**Methodology.** Hospital counts are computed at render time from the CMS TEAM participant roster vendored in this repository (`data/territoryHospitals.json`, March 2026 extract used sitewide).^1^ Editorial copy cites the June 2026 quarterly update; live counts reconcile to those locked anchors (see methods note in §02). Estimated lower-extremity joint replacement (LEJR) volume is approximately **17,500** episodes annually at California TEAM hospitals — more than **14%** of national TEAM LEJR volume.^2^ Kaiser Permanente is the largest single system on the California roster.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-glance
glance <- tibble::tibble(
  Signal = c(
    "Mandated hospitals",
    "CBSAs",
    "Medicare beneficiaries",
    "HRRP penalty rate",
    "Est. annual LEJR"
  ),
  `California TEAM` = c(
    as.character(SCOPE_N),
    as.character(SCOPE_CBSA_N),
    editorial$medicare,
    editorial$hrrp,
    editorial$lejr
  ),
  `Why it matters` = c(
    editorial$why_hospitals,
    "Multi-market operating complexity",
    "Scale of covered lives",
    "Readmission risk under episode accountability",
    "Volume concentration"
  )
)
knitr::kable(glance)
```

# 02 · Where the mandate sits: CBSAs and regions

## Figure 1 · Mandated hospitals by CBSA

San Francisco–Oakland–Fremont leads California with **`r sf_n`** TEAM hospitals. Riverside–San Bernardino–Ontario (**`r riverside_n`**) is the second-largest TEAM CBSA nationally after New York.^1^

```{r}
#| label: fig-cbsa
#| fig-cap: "CMS TEAM-mandated hospitals in California by CBSA."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of TEAM hospitals by California CBSA"
#| out-width: "100%"
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig1-cbsa.png")
```

*Figure 1. CMS TEAM-mandated hospitals in California by CBSA. Source: CMS TEAM participant list; live count from repo roster extract.^1^*

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cbsa
cbsa_table |>
  transmute(
    CBSA = cbsa_label,
    Hospitals = hospitals,
    `Share (%)` = share_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

**Note on Greater Los Angeles.** Much of Greater Los Angeles is **not** organized as a CMS TEAM CBSA selection in the same way as the Bay Area or Inland Empire markets; the Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim row on Figure 1 reflects the limited TEAM footprint CMS listed for that CBSA, not the full hospital inventory of Southern California.^3^ Riverside–San Bernardino–Ontario (**`r riverside_n`**) is the operational center of gravity for Southern California TEAM volume outside San Diego.

## Figure 2 · Mandated hospitals by region

Bay Area and Inland Empire together account for **`r bay_inland_share`%** of California’s TEAM hospitals (`r bay_inland_n` of `r SCOPE_N`).

```{r}
#| label: fig-region
#| fig-cap: "CMS TEAM-mandated hospitals by California region."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of TEAM hospitals by California region"
#| out-width: "100%"
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig2-region.png")
```

*Figure 2. Regional concentration of California TEAM hospitals. X-axis label: “Number of TEAM-mandated sites per region.” Bay Area = San Francisco–Oakland–Fremont + San Jose–Sunnyvale–Santa Clara. Inland Empire = Riverside–San Bernardino–Ontario. Source: CMS participant list; Rainfall regional rollup.^1^*

```{r}
region_table |>

```

**Methods note (roster provenance).** `r reconciliation_note`

# 03 · Episode-cost exposure (Rainfall method)

Rainfall’s **California Episode Economics Analysis** applies a **17-system** exposure method to compare relative modeled episode-cost pressure across California TEAM systems.^4^ Figure 3 is **illustrative** of relative bands from that method — not a hospital-specific CMS reconciliation. Episode-cost dollars are **not** stored as a reproducible CSV in this repository; the chart uses a unitless relative index and is labeled accordingly.

**Methods note (exposure dollars).** `r exposure_data_gap_note`

Advisory Board’s Daily Briefing on TEAM readiness (August 18, 2025) is cited only for **external range context** on how hospitals are discussing first-cycle exposure; it is **not** a formal TEAM Financial Impact Model PDF and is not the methodology source for Figure 3.^5^

Under the Rainfall method, **Zuckerberg San Francisco General** sits in a **low modeled dollar-exposure** band relative to peer California TEAM systems.^4^

```{r}
#| label: tbl-exposure-method
knitr::kable(
  exposure_methodology,
  caption = "Illustrative methodology — Rainfall California Episode Economics Analysis (17-system method)"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-exposure
#| fig-cap: "Illustrative relative episode-cost exposure across example California TEAM systems."
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of illustrative relative episode-cost exposure by example system"
#| out-width: "100%"
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig3-exposure.png")
```

*Figure 3. Illustrative relative exposure index from Rainfall’s California Episode Economics Analysis (17-system method).^4^ Advisory Board Daily Briefing (Aug 18, 2025) used for industry range context only — not the figure methodology.^5^ \*Zuckerberg San Francisco General: low modeled exposure under the Rainfall method.^4^*

# 04 · Readmissions pressure: HRRP and LEJR

California TEAM hospitals face elevated readmission penalty prevalence: **55.2%** with an HRRP penalty versus **48.1%** nationally.^6^

```{r}
#| label: fig-hrrp
#| fig-cap: "HRRP penalty prevalence, California TEAM hospitals vs national IPPS average."
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart comparing HRRP penalty rates"
#| out-width: "62%"
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig4-hrrp.png")
```

*Figure 4. Share of hospitals with an HRRP penalty. Source: CMS HRRP FY2025 supplemental data (dataset 9n3s-kdb3).^6^ Rates reused from site chart tooling; raw hospital-level HRRP CSV is not vendored in this repo. Provenance: `r hrrp_provenance`*

Hip/knee replacement excess readmission ratios remain a core LEJR risk lens for TEAM hospitals managing orthopedic episode bundles.^7^ Prior mandatory joint-replacement experience showed that shifting discharge patterns — including reductions in institutional post-acute use — can move total episode spend. Illustrative planning ranges used by operators often cite roughly a **15%** SNF-to-home-health shift corresponding to on the order of **$30–50M** in aggregate episode spend opportunity across a large multi-hospital footprint; treat as scenario planning, not a hospital-specific forecast.^8^

# 05 · What changes in PY2 (2027)

**Performance Year 2 begins in 2027.** Design elements hospitals should track:

1. **PSI-90** quality weighting is removed after PY1 (CMS-5540-F).
2. **Spinal fusion** enters TEAM episode logic with MS-DRGs **523–525** effective for discharges on or after **October 1, 2026** (FY2027 IPPS final rule).
3. **HRSN / HEP** screening and related health-equity pathway elements remain **voluntary** under the FY2026 IPPS final rule framework as implemented for TEAM.
4. **Composite Quality Score (CQS)** rolling-baseline changes discussed in **CMS-1849-P** are **proposed only** unless and until finalized — do not treat NPRM language as final policy.

Primary citations for this section are CMS rulemaking documents (TEAM final rule / IPPS packages), not secondary commentary.^2^

# 06 · Executive priorities and FAQ

## Priorities before PY2

1. **Lock the roster truth.** Reconcile internal hospital lists to the CMS June 2026 TEAM participant file by CCN and CBSA.^1^
2. **Quantify LEJR and inbound spinal-fusion exposure** with physician and post-acute partners before October 2026 DRG go-live.
3. **Readmissions operations.** Pair HRRP surveillance with TEAM episode dashboards so orthopedic and medical readmissions are not managed in separate silos.^6^
4. **Post-acute network design.** Revisit SNF vs home-health routing against quality and cost, using historical CJR/BPCI lessons without copying outdated playbooks.^8^
5. **Quality measure transitions.** Retire PSI-90-centric TEAM narratives after PY1; prepare spinal-fusion coding and documentation workflows for FY2027.

## FAQ

**Why do some materials say 110 California TEAM hospitals instead of 107?**  
Use **107** as the operating count aligned to the CMS June 2026 participant list.^1^ Older decks or secondary tallies sometimes still show **110**. The **107 vs 110** clarification appears **only here** in the FAQ — not elsewhere in this paper — to avoid repeating a correction readers do not need twice.

**Is Greater Los Angeles “in TEAM”?**  
Only to the limited extent CMS listed TEAM participants in the Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim CBSA. Do not equate the metro’s full hospital market with TEAM mandate status.^3^

**Where should finance teams start on exposure?**  
Start with Rainfall’s California Episode Economics Analysis method for relative system pressure,^4^ then layer hospital-specific claims once available — not with a generic national briefing alone.^5^

```{r}
#| label: tbl-directory
hospitals |>
  dplyr::group_by(cbsa_label) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Hospitals = dplyr::n(),
    `Named hospitals` = paste(hospital, collapse = " · "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Hospitals), cbsa_label) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
